subject: Segmentation provenance — compact walkthrough and deliverables
body:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@bigbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Segmentation provenance request for SOC 2

Hi Soojin,

We're preparing our SOC 2 evidence bundle and the auditor has asked for a concise provenance narrative describing how Redwood enforces tenant segmentation for Dedicated and Private deployments. They specifically want:
- A short architecture narrative (1–2 pages) that explains network/host boundaries, control plane separation, and fallback behavior.
- Network diagrams (logical + minimal physical), with callouts for where tenant traffic is isolated.
- A timestamped list of the last three configuration changes that impacted segmentation (who, what, why).
- An egress allowlist/ACL snapshot and notes on KMS boundaries.

Can you provide a compact walkthrough and artefacts we can include in the package? Preferably PDF and vector diagrams.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Information Security Analyst
BigBank Financial

--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@bigbank.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segmentation provenance request for SOC 2

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear checklist. We can assemble a compact "segmentation provenance" bundle aimed at auditors: a one-page narrative, a single-page sequence diagram for control plane vs data plane, a vector network diagram (SVG), and a CSV snapshot of egress/ACLs.

Quick Qs so we make the artefacts useful: who is the auditor contact (name/email) and do you want change metadata down to the git commit ID or just date/user/summary? We can provide both but will need to redact some internal ticket IDs if BigBank prefers.

I'll pull together a first draft and loop in our architecture and product-security leads for the change-log items.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment: segprov_compact-draft-notes.txt (plain text, 3 KB)

-- Forwarded message --
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Segmentation provenance request for SOC 2

Team — Alice from BigBank needs a compact provenance bundle for their SOC 2 auditor. Deliverables she asked for are:
- 1-page architecture narrative (auditor-friendly)
- 1-page control-vs-data plane sequence diagram
- Vector network diagram (SVG) with labeled zones for Dedicated and Private
- Timestamped change list for the last three segmentation-impacting changes (date / author / short reason)
- Egress allowlist CSV for tenant-facing egress (include port/proto/destination)
- KMS boundary statement and artifact pointing to keys in customer-managed KMS (if applicable)

Please collate existing diagrams and the most recent config snapshot. If we don't have a clean change list, pull from infra-config repo commits and the change-control ticket summaries. Annotate any redactions.

Target: send compiled bundle back to Alice by EOD Monday (29 Nov). I can do the narrative and drive the QA pass; Kimberly, can you produce the SVG and ACL CSV? Karthik, can you source the change metadata and short explanations? Marcus, please add a one-paragraph KMS boundary statement and confirm where HSM/KMS logs are retained.

Thanks — keep replies consolidated to reduce back-and-forth.

Soojin

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Segmentation provenance request for SOC 2

Soojin — I pulled the current diagrams and started a compact SVG. Attaching the working files. Notes:
- I recommend including an "interface-level egress allowlist table" (one table) that maps service -> outbound destinations, protocol, reason. That makes auditor review faster.
- For Private deployments we should call out the optional NAT/edge-colocation pattern and highlight that the control plane endpoints are in a separate VPC with strict peering rules.
- I have a draft diagram: segprov_v1.svg (vector) and a CSV template egress_matrix.csv.
- For change provenance: if Karthik can provide commit IDs we can include a redacted mapping (commit -> date -> author -> REDWOOD-CHG-XXXX) so the auditor has traceability without exposing tickets.

I'll attach: segprov_v1.svg, egress_matrix.csv, and a small readme describing what we redacted.

-Kim

Attachment: segprov_v1.svg (SVG, 160 KB)
Attachment: egress_matrix.csv (CSV, 18 KB)
Attachment: readme_redactions.txt (plain text, 1.1 KB)

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Segmentation provenance request for SOC 2

Team — pulled change metadata from infra-config repo. Proposed three change entries (formatted for inclusion):
1) 2026-10-11T08:42Z | anita_ops | tightened cross-tenant peering rules; blocked cross-VPC ephemeral port ranges (commit: a1b2c3d)
2) 2026-09-02T15:17Z | raj_patch | introduced KV-cache isolation flags for private-dedicated runtime (commit: d4e5f6g)
3) 2026-06-21T10:05Z | infra_mig | control plane partitioning update for Dedicated (commit: f7g8h9i)

I'll redact internal ticket identifiers and produce a short explanation for each. I can also produce a tiny CSV mapping commit -> date -> author -> human summary.

Karthik

Attachment: config_snapshot_20261120.txt (plain text, 4 KB)

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 07:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Segmentation provenance request for SOC 2

Added KMS boundary blurb:
- Customer data keys for Private deployments are optionally customer-managed; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS in specific regions. Key usage logs are exported to the customer's audit bucket and retained for 90 days by default (extendable).
- HSM-backed signing for control-plane certificates is used for rotation proofs; references to the rotation manifests are included in the provided change list.

I confirm the retention and can provide the log export manifest if the auditor needs it.

-Marcus

--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@bigbank.com>, security@bigbank.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segmentation provenance request for SOC 2

Alice — attaching a compact provenance bundle for your auditor. Summary of contents below and quick notes on scope.

Summary (delivered):
- segprov_compact.pdf — 2-page narrative and sequence diagram (PDF).
- segprov_v1.svg — vector network diagram with labeled zones (Dedicated/Private/Control plane).
- egress_matrix.csv — one-table egress allowlist snapshot (CSV).
- config_snapshot_20261120.txt — config snapshot used to derive change metadata.
- change_log_commits.csv (included inside PDF archive) — commit/date/author mapping (redacted ticket ids).

Notes:
- We redacted internal ticket IDs but included commit hashes for traceability; if the auditor needs ticket-level context, we can provide a redacted package under an NDA.
- KMS/HSM boundaries are documented in the KMS blurb; log-export manifests are available on request.
- This bundle intentionally focuses on network and control/data plane separation; we did not include runtime kernel specifics or proprietary perf optimizations.

Next step: if you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough for the auditor and your engineering lead to review the diagrams and change provenance. I'm available Tue/Wed morning PST.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: segprov_compact.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB); segprov_v1.svg (SVG, 160 KB); egress_matrix.csv (CSV, 18 KB); config_snapshot_20261120.txt (TXT, 4 KB)
